| [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v3 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. It has three tests on a candidate factor, at a level and for a target. (1) System: it clears the threshold criterion. (2) Description: a model in which it governs its own regimes for goals beats a device model by more than the Occam cost (Orseau et al., priced as in [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)). (3) Adaptation: its governance would change if its actions' consequences changed (Kenton et al.). It answers the circularity objection by running on candidates whose boundaries come from (1), not from agency, and it answers the permissiveness objection without the will paper's supposition. | Proposed |
